gustav.course: Follows hexsides, drawn just inside the north/west hex. From the sea at the Garigliano mouth (coastal side 1808-1909) along the Garigliano (1908-1909 ... 2308-2408, 2307-2407, 2406-2407, 2406-2507, 2406-2506), up the Gari (2405-2506, 2405-2505, 2404-2505), round Cassino on the Rapido (2504-2505, 2504-2604, 2603-2604, 2603-2704, 2703-2704), then north-east away from the river: 2703-2803, 2802-2803, 2802-2903, 2902-2903, 2903-3002, 3002-3003, leaving the photo east along the south side of 3002. Every river hexside from the sea to 2703-2704 carries it; it does not follow the Liri.

uncertain: River class: in this photo only the Garigliano (from the Liri-Gari confluence at the 2405/2406/2506 corner to the sea) is drawn in the major-river style (dark outlines, light centre, 8-11 px). The Liri, Gari, Rapido and the upper Volturno are solid blue bands with no outline (4-7 px), matching the minor-river symbol, so I recorded them as minor. This contradicts the expectation that the Liri, Rapido and Volturno are major; please cross-check with the S photo (Volturno near Capua) and with the TEC. The Gari has river-with-marsh sides (2404-2505, 2405-2505, 2405-2506, 2405-2406), which count as major anyway.

notes: Calibration: 160 label anchors read at 2-4x zoom, locally weighted homography (sigma 3 grid units) using grid.py fit_hw/apply_h with this map's parity and label offset (ngrid.py). Displaced labels (2405, 2710, 1910, 2910, 3002) were left out.

Map key (NE photo) and TEC read at zoom: minor road = cream line with black dashed edges; major road = dark grey band with cream edges; town = beige circle; city = black grid (none in this photo); minor river = solid blue line; major river = blue with dark outlines; River+Marsh hexside = river with a grey marsh band and tufts; mountain hexside = side entirely covered by the dark shading; mountain pass = ")(" across a side; landmark = small white rectangle; peak = triangle with height.

Mountain hexsides: measured as the share of 22 points along the side where at least 4 of 5 samples across it (-6..+6 px) are dark shading (mean RGB < 66). Values were bimodal (82 sides at 0.91-1.0, the rest 0.59 or less); every borderline side was checked by eye, and all sides at 1.0 in each massif were looked at.

Rivers: blue pixels within 14 px of the side at 22 points; river sides came out at 0.73-1.0 and were all checked by eye; non-river values were 0.45 or less (2009-2109 is the blue "Garigliano" lettering, not a river).

Roads: traced by eye hex by hex on 20 zoomed overlays, with extra 3-4x zooms wherever a road passes near a hex corner, then drawn back over the photo to check (z/rc*.jpg). Every road side that is also a river side is marked bridge.

Gustav Line (dark red dashes) and Bernhard Line (black dots) both follow hexsides and are drawn just inside the north/west hex; the hexes on that side carry gustav/bernhard=true. Neither crosses a hex.
Full Mountain hexes (six mountain sides inside this photo): 2502 (M. Cairo), 2601, 2806 (M. Sammucro), 2906 (M. Corno). 1802 and 1805 are wholly dark too, but their column 17 sides are off the photo.
The only road on a mountain hexside is the minor road on 2310-2410. Passes: 2601-2701, 2601-2602, 2503-2602, 2904-2905.
No cities, airfields, garrison notes or 8th Army zone in this photo. Scauri (1807) is the only port (minor-port symbol). Monte Cassino (2504) is the only landmark.
Sea: everything west of the coast is sea, including the darker teal strip along the shore. Column 18 rows 8-13 are sea; their outlines are not printed apart from the zig-zag west sides of column 19.
The numbers 1-5 printed along roads (some upside down) are road numbers, not VPs; VPs are the red circles.
A VP 1 circle at the far left (photo x~8, y~936) is in column 17 (1706), outside this transcription.
